regate_checks.b_redeploy_qa_sh_no_standalone_bash_line: PASS -- re-read lib/letflow/design/req367-cd-qa-deploy.md §1 in full (all 8 numbered steps). Every step is now prose describing purpose/target-paths/ordering (e.g. 'Move into the app directory, pull the latest commit on the checked-out branch, then capture the resulting short commit ref into a variable and print it'; 'Build the backend image using the shared, existing deploy Dockerfile... tagging the result as the QA backend's latest image'). No standalone literal command lines (previously: `cd "$APP_DIR"`, `git pull`, `docker build -f deploy/Dockerfile -t letflow-qa:latest .`, `$COMPOSE up -d --force-recreate app`, `curl -sf https://qa.bizdala.com/`) remain anywhere in §1.
regate_checks.c_cd_yml_no_literal_yaml_blocks: PASS -- re-read §2 in full (Triggers, Jobs, gate-reuse mechanism, Steps, Secret names subsections). Trigger/gate/step mechanics are described in prose (e.g. 'The workflow fires on completion of the CI workflow (named "CI"), restricted to the main branch'; 'Its connection details are drawn from three repository secrets... supplying the target host, the connecting username, and the private key'). No literal YAML key:value fragments (previously: `on: workflow_run: workflows: ["CI"], branches: [main], types: [completed]`, `if: github.event.workflow_run.conclusion == 'success'`, the SSH step's four populated input keys) remain. Secret names (QA_DEPLOY_HOST/QA_DEPLOY_USER/QA_DEPLOY_SSH_KEY) are listed as plain identifiers, not key:value syntax -- consistent with the prior gate's ruling that naming them is required by the acceptance criteria and is not itself implementation syntax.
regate_checks.f_no_implementation_code_in_new_sections: PASS -- no fenced code blocks, no bare command/YAML syntax lines found anywhere in §1 or §2 on a full re-read.
regate_checks.no_regression_spot_check: PASS -- §0 (sources consulted), §3 (why this avoids duplicating diff logic), §4 (redeploy-test.sh untouched), §5 (explicit scope), §6 (AC mapping table), §7 (six open questions) all read intact and consistent with the previously-passed version; CODE-DESIGNER's step-01 result.summary claim that only §1/§2 changed is corroborated by content inspection. §6's AC-mapping table's concrete-design-element column still accurately cites §1 steps 2-7 and §2's trigger/gate/steps content after the prose rewrite -- the mapping was already high-level (row descriptions, not literal syntax quotes) so the §1/§2 rewrite did not invalidate it.
